PullRequest.Title: chat: target dictation and voice at the clicked input
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Clicking Dictation or Voice Mode in an unfocused split chat could start capture in the previously focused input. The segmented control bypassed the normal toolbar action context.

- Forward the owning toolbar context to dictation.
- Resolve Voice Mode targets from the originating widget, sharing that path with the standalone voice action. Host-owned draft composers select their own target rather than their placeholder model; excluded or unavailable explicit inputs cannot fall back to another chat.
- Keep voice decorations and post-connect controls with the explicitly targeted, visible chat group.
- Preserve context-free keyboard routing and the existing dictation stop/cancel behavior.

Start reading at `voiceInputModeActionViewItem.ts`, then `voiceInputUtils.ts` and the draft-composer override.

## How to test

1. Open two chats in adjacent chat groups in the Agents Window.
2. Focus the left input, then click Dictation in the right input.
3. Check that dictation starts in the right input. Stop it.
4. Focus the left input again and click Voice Mode in the right input.
5. Check that the right input owns Voice Mode. While connected, clicking a different input's voice button transfers ownership; clicking the owner's button disconnects.
6. Check Enter/Space activation, context-free shortcuts, and a new-chat composer.

Real mouse clicks in an isolated Code OSS window reproduced left-input activation on the base revision and right-input activation with this change, while DOM focus stayed on the left. Both Dictation and Voice Mode were recorded before and after.

## Validation

**146 focused tests passed.** The four modified test files also passed separately (106 overlapping test cases).

```sh
# Passed: client compilation and type checking
pnpm run gulp compile-client

# Passed: 121 tests
./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/voiceInputMode.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/actions/chatSpeechToTextActions.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/agentsVoice/test/browser/voiceModeActions.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/voiceClient/voiceInputUtils.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/voiceClient/voiceInputDecorations.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/test/browser/chat/sharedChatInputComposer.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/dictationSession.test.ts

# Passed: 25 tests
./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/voiceBridge.test.ts

# Passed: all four files in isolation
./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --isolate \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/voiceInputMode.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/agentsVoice/test/browser/voiceModeActions.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/voiceClient/voiceInputUtils.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/test/browser/chat/sharedChatInputComposer.test.ts

# Passed: all 11 changed TypeScript files
git diff --name-only HEAD^ HEAD -- '*.ts' | xargs pnpm run oxlint

# Passed
pnpm run valid-layers-check
```

Live validation covers activation ownership, not end-to-end transcription. The default local transcription model stalled during preparation; the cloud dictation backend was then used for the paired recordings. The voice service also reported a connection failure, so the recordings demonstrate targeting during activation, not a successful spoken conversation. Full smoke/integration suites and other operating systems were not tested.

Scenarios.Scenario: Start, stop, or cancel dictation from a clicked split-chat input, including Enter/Space activation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Toolbar dispatch resolves one owning widget and runs the existing global dictation lifecycle. Capture waits for microphone acquisition and backend session setup. Local model download/load proceeds in the utility process while capture buffers audio; usable transcription waits for readiness. Stopping flushes audio, finalizes the backend, and optionally awaits language-model cleanup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire microphone stream and initialize audio capture.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One stream acquisition per accepted start.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same acquisition and capture sequence, but the segmented control selected the last-focused widget.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Lazily create the local transcription utility worker.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One worker on first local use or after existing cancellation/termination resets it; shared across requests while alive.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same lazy worker lifetime and creation count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Worker creation precedes local backend start; model preparation then runs asynchronously.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start one local transcription session, query status, and forward audio to the utility process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One start, one initial status query plus one preparation re-query when needed, and one push per audio chunk.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Start/status responses precede capture setup; subsequent chunk delivery drives transcription.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: For cloud dictation, authenticate and open one transcription WebSocket; optionally request final language-model cleanup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One socket/session per accepted cloud start, messages per audio chunk, and at most one optional cleanup operation per finalization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same network operations and finalization ordering.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cloud connection and initialization precede capture; enabled cleanup delays final text.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One active dictation session per window; transport work scales with recorded audio chunks and transcript length, not the number of split inputs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Global speech-service state and pending start/stop guards admit only one session. Preparation is asynchronous in one local worker; start/stop sequencing is unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Local runtime/model preparation uses the existing cache directory and model selection; cold downloads and warm model reuse are unchanged. Cloud sockets retain their existing per-session lifecycle. The diff adds no cache or negative-cache policy.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed dispatch only supplies toolbar context; the action, lifecycle guards, local proxy, and cloud client were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cold model preparation and network duration are deployment-dependent, but their frequency and scheduling do not change.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: ownership changes without adding capture, subprocess, IPC, or network fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Connect Voice Mode from an explicit input or context-free keyboard command
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Resolve the destination, then run the existing controller connection path: availability check, authentication, persisted transcript loading, and hosted WebSocket or BYOK setup. Recording/listening follows connection according to the existing hold/hands-free behavior.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check configured BYOK availability through the speech provider; initialize a live session when selected.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One availability check per accepted connect, reused by _connectGptLive; BYOK session setup only when configured and available.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same check, reuse, and conditional setup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Availability is awaited before remaining connection setup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve GitHub authentication sessions through the authentication service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One getSessions call per accepted connection attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before the client transport connects.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and parse the user's persisted transcript for the last turn and prior timeline.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two sequential loadTurns calls when a user login exists; each reads the file before applying its result limit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same two reads, full-file parsing, and limits; this is not introduced or amplified by target resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both existing reads are on connection startup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Establish hosted voice transport or the selected BYOK live connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One selected connection path per admitted attempt; existing reconnect budgeting remains unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same transport selection and connection count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Connection/session initialization is required before listening.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One connection attempt per controller. Persisted transcript reads scale with that user's file size; session-context construction scales with eligible active/recent sessions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Controller isConnecting/isConnected guards prevent simultaneous accepted connects; availability, authentication, and transcript loading are awaited sequentially. The diff does not introduce parallel connection bursts.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Explicit input resolution now uses the widget directly instead of an ambient routing command; that command is local state lookup, not an expensive service read. Context-free routing remains. BYOK availability is cached for the subsequent setup call. Transcript file reads remain uncached and unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both changed callers and helper were traced through controller guards and client setup.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Authentication, transcript size, and transport latency vary; no new boundary count or critical-path placement was established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression or concrete performance-regression fix: routing changes and removal of a local command do not establish a substantive performance mechanism.

Scenarios.Scenario: Transfer an already-connected Voice Mode session to another visible chat group
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Resolve the clicked widget, update the existing controller target, and activate that session. Activation may flush buffered audio and sends session context before any pending narration. It does not reconnect.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Build grouped session context and serialize changed transport payloads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One context build for an explicit connected activation; hosted delta sending and BYOK grounding/briefing comparisons suppress unchanged transport data.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The previous retarget helper also called setTargetSession and activateSession, reaching the same context-building and flush path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Context is flushed before pending narration; not awaited for a new connection.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send changed grouped session context and, when warranted, request narration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Grouped delta rather than one message per session; existing transcript/narration deduplication applies.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same activation transport behavior, targeting the ambient session rather than the clicked one.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Conditionally acquire/load nonresident eligible chat models through the chat service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One load per missing resource after retained-reference, resident-model, and in-flight guards; legacy adoptable sessions are skipped.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same conditional model-loading path and per-resource guards were reached by activateSession and context construction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous detail loading can later update context/narration; activation does not await it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One explicit activation per user gesture. Context includes eligible sessions after archived/old-session filtering; model loading is at most once per missing eligible resource while in flight or retained.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No reconnection on transfer. Model loads are coalesced per resource, not globally limited; the diff does not increase collection fan-out or remove coalescing.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing resident models, eager reference map, in-flight set, buffered response identity checks, hosted deltas, and BYOK grounding comparisons remain. The diff changes only which input is authoritative.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both old and new helpers invoke the same controller operations; their downstream serialization, network, and load guards were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Eligible session count and pending response sizes vary, but no changed operation frequency or cardinality was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: existing expensive activation behavior is preserved rather than newly introduced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Select a host-owned new-chat composer as the Voice Mode destination
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The widget override checks host eligibility, enters a synchronous voice transition, selects the registered composer, disposes the transition, and returns the shared draft sentinel. Existing connection/listening and eventual spoken-query submission follow.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One registered composer selection per explicit gesture; constant-time Set membership and one observable update. No new session is created by resolving the destination.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Selection is synchronous. Existing composer-change observers consume the transition to avoid disconnect/reconnect during intentional transfer. Backend connection concurrency is unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The existing composer registry owns mounted composers and removes them on disposal. The new resolver neither adds registry entries nor caches destinations; it resolves the current host each invocation. The temporary transition is disposed in finally.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: resolver, target service, registration cleanup, and composer-change observer were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Observable notification cost depends on mounted surfaces, but no heavy operation, retained resource growth, or extra connection was introduced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: bounded ownership bookkeeping, with excluded hosts rejected before capture.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render voice glow, transcript, and post-connect controls on the explicitly targeted visible split group
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Visibility/ownership observables select the existing decoration surface. Connected owning surfaces run the existing requestAnimationFrame glow and transcript DOM updates; unrelated or hidden surfaces stop animation. Controls update synchronously through existing context keys.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read existing audio analyser state, render the glow, replace latest-turn DOM, and scan the transcript scroll node.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One frame loop per visible owning decoration surface; transcript updates render only the latest visible turn. Unrelated groups do not start frame loops.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same decoration renderer ran on the active surface matching currentVoiceInputResource; the diff allows the explicitly targeted visible surface to render even when unfocused.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs on the renderer frame/update path; no capture or service operation is required.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Mounted chat views receive existing subscriptions; active rendering is restricted to visible views matching the concrete target, normally one chat group. The voice transcript buffer is already bounded to two turns.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing per-surface frame-loop guard prevents duplicate scheduling; losing ownership, hiding the view, disconnecting, or disposal cancels the loop. No subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network boundary is introduced by these subscriptions.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The new derived ownership observable is lifecycle-owned by the existing view; renderer/analyser buffer reuse and the existing bounded transcript buffer are unchanged. No new DOM tree or heavyweight renderer is constructed by the diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: ownership predicate, visibility setters, shared decorations, frame cancellation, and transcript buffer bound were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Frame cost depends on hardware and the number of views displaying the same target; the diff deliberately moves necessary rendering to the destination, without demonstrated pathological amplification.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: intentional destination rendering uses the existing guarded, disposable decoration path.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over the complete 11-file inventory and every diff page against base 810d74bc3f30764cad86132ffcdf22e509b9913f. Traced targeting, dictation lifecycle, connection setup, connected transfer, draft ownership, and visible decorations. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regressions or concrete performance-fix provenance signals qualified. Static read-only review; no profiling performed. The host truncated the requested performance guide output, while learned mechanism guidance was available.
